mom_12_1: Each month, buys the 10 stocks that rose most over the past year (skipping the last month).
Winners tend to keep winning for a while because news sinks in slowly.
mom_residual_12_1: Each month, buys the 10 stocks with the strongest rise of their own, after removing the part that came from the whole market moving.
Momentum that isn't just 'the market went up' is steadier and crashes less.
mom_52wk_high: Each month, buys the 10 stocks closest to their highest price of the past year.
Investors hesitate to buy near a high, so good news gets priced in late.
mom_frog_in_pan: Among the 30 strongest stocks of the past year, buys the 10 whose rise came in many small steps rather than a few big jumps.
Slow, steady gains go unnoticed (like a frog in warming water), so they last longer.
mom_risk_adjusted: Each month, buys the 10 stocks with the best past-year gain per unit of volatility.
A calm rise is a more reliable signal than a wild one.
mom_vol_managed: 12-month momentum, but invests less money when the picks have been swinging a lot.
Momentum crashes tend to come in volatile markets, so stepping back then should help.
mom_bear_switch: Holds the 10 strongest stocks, but after a two-year market fall switches to holding every stock.
Momentum often crashes when markets rebound after a long fall.
mom_time_series_stock: Holds every stock whose past-year gain beat what cash (T-bills) earned; the rest sits in cash.
Only own what's actually going up; step aside from what isn't.
mom_intermediate_12_7: Buys the 10 stocks that did best from 12 to 7 months ago, ignoring the last six months.
Some research says the older part of the trend predicts better.
mom_acceleration: Buys the 10 rising stocks whose last six months beat the six before by the most.
A trend that's speeding up may have more to run.
mom_consistent: Buys the strongest stocks of the past year, but only those that were up in at least 8 of the 11 months.
Gains spread across many months are less likely to be one lucky event.
mom_clenow_regression: Each week, ranks stocks by how steeply and smoothly they've climbed over 90 days and holds the top 10, with trend and crash filters.
A popular book method: buy the cleanest uptrends, drop them when the trend breaks.
rev_1w: Each Friday, buys the 10 stocks that fell most over the week, for one week.
rev_1m: Each month, buys the 10 stocks that fell most over the past month.
Big one-month drops sometimes overshoot and recover.
rev_residual_1w: Each Friday, buys the 10 stocks that fell most compared with what the market alone would explain.
A stock-specific drop with no market reason is more likely to reverse.
rev_overnight_momentum: Buys the 10 stocks that gained most between close and next open over the past month.
Overnight moves are said to reflect steady buying that continues.
rev_intraday_losers: Buys the 10 stocks that lost most during trading hours (open to close) over the past month.
Daytime selling is said to be noise that later reverses.
overnight_only_hold: Buys every stock at the close and sells at the next open, every day.
A famous finding: most of the market's gains came overnight. A test, not a usable strategy.
lowvol_252: Each month, holds the 20 calmest stocks of the past year.
Calm stocks have historically done about as well as wild ones, with smaller drops.
lowbeta_bab: Each month, holds the 20 stocks that move least with the market.
Investors overpay for high-beta stocks, so low-beta ones are often cheap.
low_idio_vol: Each month, holds the 20 stocks with the smallest moves of their own (not counting market moves).
Stocks with big individual swings tend to be overpriced lottery tickets.
lottery_max_avoid: Holds every stock except the 20% with the biggest single-day jump last month.
Stocks that just had a huge day attract gamblers and later lag.
low_realized_skew: Each month, holds the 20 stocks with the fewest big up-spikes recently.
People overpay for the chance of a big jump.
min_variance: Each month, picks the mix of stocks (max 10% each) that would have swung the least together.
Combining calm, unrelated stocks gives a smoother ride.
nr7_breakout: After the quietest day of the last 7, buys if the price breaks above that day's high (in an uptrend).
Quiet days often come before a big move.
squeeze_breakout: After at least 5 days of very tight price swings, buys on the first strong push upward.
Volatility comes in cycles: squeezes tend to end in a burst.
keltner_trend: Buys when the price closes well above its recent average plus two typical daily ranges; sells below the average.
A strong push out of the usual range often starts a trend.
wide_range_followthrough: Buys after a day with an unusually wide range that closes near its high, in an uptrend.
A powerful day signals buyers in control.
vol_open_breakout: Buys during the day if the price rises half of yesterday's range above today's open; sells at the close.
An old day-trading method (Larry Williams). Trades inside the day.
ibs_reversion: Buys an uptrending stock that closes near the bottom of its day's range; sells when it closes near the top or after 5 days.
Weak closes in strong stocks tend to bounce.
consec_down_days: Buys an uptrending stock after 3 lower closes in a row; sells on the first up close.
Short pullbacks in an uptrend usually don't last.
residual_zscore_reversion: Buys when a stock has fallen unusually far over 5 days compared with the market, in an uptrend.
Extreme stock-specific drops tend to snap back.
variance_ratio_dip: Buys 10-day lows, but only in stocks that historically tend to reverse rather than trend.
Buying dips works better where prices tend to bounce.
cs_ibs_daily: Every day, holds the 5 uptrending stocks that closed weakest in their day's range, for one day.
Same bounce idea as IBS, as a daily basket.
drawdown_turnaround: Buys a stock at least 30% below its high once it climbs back above a rising 50-day average.
Beaten-down stocks that start trending up again can recover strongly.
gap_up_continuation: Buys a stock that opens 4%+ higher on heavy volume and holds its gains.
Big news gaps tend to keep moving in the same direction.
gap_down_reversal: Buys an uptrending stock that opens 3%+ lower but closes above its open, on normal volume.
A drop with no real news that recovers during the day is often a false alarm.
gap_fill_intraday: Buys at the open after a 2%+ gap down in an uptrend; sells the same day at the close.
Gaps often partly fill during the day. Trades inside the day.
shock_drift_up: Buys after an unusually large stock-specific rise on heavy volume; holds 20 days.
Prices underreact to real news and keep drifting.
shock_reversal_no_volume: Buys after an unusually large stock-specific fall on light volume; holds 10 days.
A big fall without heavy volume is more likely noise than news.
market_crash_rebound: When the market falls 3% or more in a day, buys every stock for 5 days.
turn_of_month: Holds stocks only around the last and first trading days of each month; cash otherwise.
Paychecks and fund flows arrive at month-end.
halloween: Holds stocks from November to April and cash from May to October.
A centuries-old saying: winter months have historically been stronger.
month_seasonality_cs: Each month, buys the 10 stocks that did best in that calendar month over the past 5 years.
Some stocks repeat seasonal patterns (earnings timing, demand cycles).
dec_tax_loss_rebound: In mid-December, buys the 10 worst stocks of the year and holds them to the end of January.
Investors dump losers for tax reasons in December; the selling stops in January.
santa_rally: Holds stocks only for the last days of December and first days of January.
The holiday period has historically been strong.
opex_week: Holds stocks only during the week of monthly options expiration.
Option hedging flows are said to push prices up that week.
weekday_skip_monday: Holds stocks every day except over the weekend into Monday.
Mondays have historically been the weakest day.
quarter_end_winners: Buys the quarter's 10 best stocks in its last week.
Fund managers buy winners before quarter-end to look good in reports.
beta_rotation_breadth: Holds the 20 most market-sensitive stocks when most stocks are in uptrends, the 20 least when few are.
Be aggressive in strong markets and defensive in weak ones.
breadth_200d_regime: Holds every stock while more than half are above their 200-day average; cash when fewer than 40% are.
When most stocks are in downtrends, the market is risky.
nh_nl_regime: Holds stocks while more are hitting 52-week highs than lows; cash otherwise.
More new lows than highs signals a weakening market.
breadth_thrust: After a sudden swing from few to most stocks rising, holds every stock for 3 months.
A rare signal (Zweig) that has marked the start of big rallies.
breadth_washout_buy: When fewer than 10% of stocks are above their 20-day average, buys every stock for a month.
Extreme selling is often near a bottom.
ad_line_divergence: Steps into cash when the market is near its high but fewer stocks are rising.
A rally led by fewer and fewer stocks is fragile.
market_absorption_ratio: Steps into cash when stocks suddenly start moving together much more than usual.
When everything moves as one, the market is fragile (Kritzman et al.).
market_turbulence: Steps into cash when daily moves become statistically unusual compared with the past 3 years.
Unusual market behaviour often comes before big drops.
dual_momentum_top10: Holds the 10 strongest stocks of the past year, but only those that also beat cash; the rest in cash.
Combines 'best of the group' with 'actually going up' (Antonacci).
protective_breadth_mom: Holds the 10 strongest stocks, moving more into cash as more stocks turn negative.
Weak breadth is a warning, so reduce risk gradually.
canary_universe: Holds the 10 strongest stocks only while both the S&P 500 and the average stock have positive momentum.
Use the market as a canary in the coal mine (Keller).
winners_on_dips: Each Friday, buys the 5 strongest-trend stocks that fell most this week; holds 2 weeks.
Buy strong stocks when they're briefly on sale.
trend_pullback_ema: In a strong uptrend, buys after the price touches its 20-day average and then turns up.
high_near_52wh_pullback: Buys a stock near its 52-week high after a 3%+ dip; sells at a new high or after 10 days.
Strong stocks' small dips are usually bought quickly.
ma_slope_trend_strength: Buys when a stock's last 20 days moved mostly in one direction (up) above its 50-day average.
Clean, efficient trends are more likely to continue than choppy ones.
mom_top_trend_exit: Buys the strongest stocks monthly, but sells any that close below their 100-day average.
Keep the winners, cut those whose trend breaks.
amihud_illiquid: Each month, holds the 20 stocks whose price moves most per dollar traded.
Investors want extra return for holding harder-to-trade stocks.
high_volume_premium: Each month, buys the 10 stocks whose trading volume suddenly jumped without a big price move.
Unusual volume draws attention and new buyers to a stock (Gervais, Kaniel & Mingelgrin).
obv_accumulation: Buys when on-balance volume hits a new high while the price hasn't yet.
Volume can lead price when big buyers are quietly accumulating.
chaikin_money_flow: Buys when the Chaikin money-flow indicator turns clearly positive in an uptrend.
Closes near the day's high on heavy volume show buying pressure.
volume_dryup_pullback: In an uptrend, after 3 down days on light volume, buys the first up day on heavy volume.
Pullbacks without heavy selling are healthy pauses.
corr_spike_filter: Steps into cash when stocks move unusually together and the market is falling.
High correlation in a falling market signals panic.
dispersion_mom_switch: Holds the 10 strongest stocks when stocks' returns differ a lot; holds every stock otherwise.
Momentum works best when winners and losers really separate.
low_corr_stocks: Each month, holds the 20 stocks least correlated with the market.
Stocks that march to their own drum diversify a portfolio.
first_new_high_after_base: First new high after a base
Buys a stock's first 52-week high after 3 months without one; sells below the 50-day average.
Breaking out of a long base can start a new leg up.
universe_entry: Buys stocks that just entered the 100 biggest, holds them for a quarter.
Newly big companies attract index and fund buying.
near_52wk_low_avoid: Holds every stock except those within 5% of their 52-week low.
Stocks near their lows often keep falling.
composite_mom_lowvol_52wh: Each month, holds the 15 stocks with the best average rank on momentum, low volatility and closeness to the 52-week high.
Mixing several proven ideas spreads the risk of any one failing.
trend_lowvol: Each month, holds the 20 calmest stocks among those above their 200-day average.
Low volatility without the falling knives.
trend_vote_5: Holds stocks where at least 4 of 5 trend checks agree; sells when 2 or fewer do.
Several signals agreeing should mean fewer false alarms.
site_lineup_vote: Holds a stock when at least 3 of the site's own on-site strategies are holding it.
If several of our strategies agree, the signal should be stronger.
mom_breadth_filter: Holds the 10 strongest stocks only while more than half of stocks are above their 200-day average.
Avoid momentum's crashes in weak markets.
factor_rotation_mom: Each month, switches to whichever of three styles (momentum, low volatility, near-high) did best over 6 months.
multi_horizon_trend_score: Holds stocks that are up over 1, 3, 6 and 12 months; sells when 2 or more turn negative.
A trend confirmed on every timescale is more reliable.
inv_vol_universe: Holds every stock, putting more money in calm ones and less in wild ones.
A simple form of risk parity: each stock contributes similar risk.
vol_target_mom: The composite strategy, investing less when it's been swinging more than 12% a year.
Keep the ride steady by sizing down in rough patches.
drawdown_brake: Holds every stock, but halves the position after a 10% fall until the market makes a new 3-month high.
Cut risk when losing, rebuild when the market recovers.
breadth_scaled_exposure: Invests more the larger the share of stocks above their 200-day average.
Scale risk with the health of the market.
